metadata.title: Moser-Tardos Algorithm with small number of random bits
metadata.authors: Endre Csoka, Lukasz Grabowski, Andras Mathe, Oleg Pikhurko, Konstantinos Tyros

nodes.name: Local rule and colouring problem
nodes.statement: A local rule for a digraph $G$ is a function $\mathbf R$ on $V(G)$ with $\mathbf R(x)\subset b^{\Var(x)}$ (and $\mathbf R(x)=b^{\emptyset}$ when $\Var(x)=\emptyset$). A colouring problem is a pair $(G,\mathbf R)$.

nodes.name: Satisfying colouring
nodes.statement: A function $f\in b^{V(G)}$ satisfies $\mathbf R$ if for every $x\in V(G)$ the restriction $\res_x(f)\in \mathbf R(x)$.

nodes.name: Dependency digraph $\Rel(G)$
nodes.statement: $\Rel(G)$ is the symmetric digraph on $V(G)$ with edge $(x,y)$ iff $\Var_G(x)\cap \Var_G(y)\neq \emptyset$; self-loops allowed.

nodes.name: Bad set $\B_{\mathbf R}(f)$
nodes.statement: $\B_{\mathbf R}(f):=\{x\in V(G):\res_x(f)\in \mathbf R^c(x)\}$, the set of clauses violated by $f$.

nodes.name: Independence function and $\IB(f)$
nodes.statement: $\I_G:\Pow(V)\to\Pow(V)$ assigns to each $X$ a maximal independent subset of $X$ in $G$; we set $\IB(f):=\I_{\Rel(G)}(\B_{\mathbf R}(f))$.

nodes.name: $r$-sparse partition
nodes.statement: A partition $\pi$ of $V(G)$ is $r$-sparse if for every $x\in V(G)$ all distinct points of $N_G(x,r)$ lie in different parts of $\pi$.

nodes.name: Moser-Tardos tuple
nodes.statement: A triple $\cal M=(G,\mathbf R,\pi)$ where $G$ is a digraph, $\mathbf R$ a local rule on $G$, and $\pi$ a partition of $V(G)$.

nodes.name: Subexponential growth class $\subexp(\nn,\eps,d)$
nodes.statement: The class of digraphs $G$ with $\maxdeg(G)\le d$ and $|N_G(x,3\nn)|\le (1+\eps)^{\nn}$ for all $x\in V(G)$.

nodes.name: Class $\colsubexp(\nn,d,\de)$
nodes.statement: Class of finite colouring problems $(G,\mathbf R)$ with $G\in \subexp(\nn,\eps,d)$ and $\max_x |\mathbf R^c(x)|/b^{|\Var(x)|}\le 1/((\me\De)^{1+\delta} b^{\eps d})$.

nodes.name: Canvas $\Canvas(G)$ and $G$-forest
nodes.statement: $\Canvas(G)$ has vertex set $V(G)\times \NN$ with edges $((x,i),(y,i+1))$ for $(x,y)\in E(\Rel(G))$. A $G$-forest $\cal F$ is a subdigraph of $\Canvas(G)$ with each vertex in-degree $\le 1$.

nodes.name: $\cal M$-landscape
nodes.statement: An $\cal M$-landscape is $\cal L=(\cal F,\prev)$ with $\cal F$ an independent $G$-forest and $\prev(x,i)\in \mathbf R^c(x)$ for $(x,i)\in V(\cal F)$.

nodes.name: Finalised landscape
nodes.statement: A finalised $\cal M$-landscape is $(\cal F,\prev,\final)$ with $(\cal F,\prev)$ an $\cal M$-landscape of finite height and $\final\in b^{V(G)}$.

nodes.name: $\used_{\cal L}$ and $\unused$ functions
nodes.statement: $\used_{\cal L}(x)$ lists $\prev(y_j,s_j)(x)$ over $(y_j,s_j)\in V(\cal F)$ with $x\in \Var(y_j)$ in increasing $s_j$ order, then $\final(x)$. $\unused$ records the remaining bits.

nodes.name: $\De$-labelled tree
nodes.statement: A finite directed tree where each vertex has in-degree 0 or 1, and out-edges at each vertex carry distinct labels in $\{0,\ldots,\De-1\}$.

nodes.name: $\pi$-unique set and landscape restriction $\Res_U$
nodes.statement: $U\subset V(G)$ is $\pi$-unique if $S_\pi$ is injective on $U$; $\Res_U(\cal M)$ and $\Res_U(\cal L)$ restrict the Moser-Tardos tuple and landscape to $U$ via $S_\pi$.

nodes.name: Equivalent landscapes
nodes.statement: Finalised $\cal M$-landscapes $\cal L,\cal K$ are equivalent if $|V(\cal L)|=|V(\cal K)|$ and $\used_{\cal L}=\used_{\cal K}$.

nodes.name: Borel digraph and Borel local rule
nodes.statement: $G=(V,\mathcal B,E)$ is a Borel digraph if $(V,\mathcal B)$ is standard Borel and $E\subset V^2$ Borel. A local rule $\mathbf R$ is Borel if its encoding $\ell_{\mathbf R}:V\to \Pow(b^\pi)$ via a Borel 2-sparse partition is Borel.

nodes.name: Lovasz Local Lemma
nodes.statement: If $G$ is a digraph, $\De=\maxdeg(\Rel(G))$, and $1-|\mathbf R(x)|/b^{|\Var(x)|}<1/(\me\De)$ for every $x$, then there is $f\in b^{V(G)}$ satisfying $\mathbf R$.

nodes.name: Main theorem (subexponential MTA)
nodes.statement: Under $G\in \subexp(\nn,\eps,d)$, $3\nn$-sparse $\pi$, and $\max_x |\mathbf R^c(x)|/b^{|\Var(x)|}\le 1/((\me\De)^{1+\delta} b^{\eps d})$, there is $K=K(b,\de,d,|\pi|)$ with $\Pr_{\rnd}(\max_x h^\infty_{\cal M,\rnd}(x)\ge m)\le K(m+1)^{|\pi|}/(\me\De)^{\de m}$.
conclusions: $\exists K=K(b,\de,d,|\pi|)$ such that for all $m\in\NN$: $\Pr_{\rnd}(\max_{x\in V(G)} h^\infty_{\cal M,\rnd}(x)\ge m)\le K(m+1)^{|\pi|}/(\me\De)^{\de m}$

nodes.name: Classical MTA bound (interlude)
nodes.statement: For finite $G$, $\pi$ all singletons, and $\be\le 1/(\me\De)^{1+\delta}$: $\Pr_{\rnd}(|V(\cal L^k_{\cal M,\rnd})|=m)\le d|V(G)|(m+1)^{|V(G)|}/(\me\De)^{\delta m}$.

nodes.name: Main analysis theorem
nodes.statement: Same hypotheses as Theorem~\ref{thm-main}: there is $K(b,\de,d,|\pi|)$ with $\Pr_{\rnd}(\max_x h^k_{\cal M,\rnd}(x)\ge m)\le K(m+1)^{|\pi|}/(\me\De)^{\de m}$ for all $m,k$.
conclusions: $\exists K=K(b,\de,d,|\pi|)$ such that for all $m,k\in\NN$: $\Pr_{\rnd}(\max_{x\in V(G)} h^k_{\cal M,\rnd}(x)\ge m)\le K(m+1)^{|\pi|}/(\me\De)^{\de m}$

nodes.name: Borel Lovasz Local Lemma (subexponential growth)
nodes.statement: If $(G,\mathbf R)$ is a Borel colouring problem with $G\in \subexp(\nn,\eps,d)$ and $\max_x b^{\eps d}|\mathbf R^c(x)|/b^{|\Var(x)|}<1/(\me\De)$, then there exists a Borel satisfying colouring $f\in b^{V(G)}$.
assumptions: $(G,\mathbf R)$ is a Borel colouring problem

nodes.name: Linear-time deterministic algorithm for $\colsubexp$
nodes.statement: For each $(\nn,d,\de)$ there is a sequential deterministic algorithm that, given $(G,\mathbf R)\in \colsubexp(\nn,d,\de)$, finds a satisfying assignment in time $O(|V(G)|)$.
conclusions: $\exists$ deterministic sequential algorithm finding satisfying assignment in time $O(|V(G)|)$

nodes.name: Predecessor lemma
nodes.statement: If $(x,i+1)\in V(\cal F_{\cal M,\rnd})$ then there exists $(y,i)\in V(\cal F_{\cal M,\rnd})$ with $\Var_G(x)\cap \Var_G(y)\neq \emptyset$ ($x=y$ allowed).

nodes.name: Used bits recovered from landscape
nodes.statement: $\used_{\cal L^k_{\cal M,\rnd}} = \used^k_{\cal M,\rnd}$ for all $k\in\NN$ and $\rnd\in b^{\pi\times \NN}$.

nodes.name: Length identities for $\used$ and $\varcount$
nodes.statement: $\len(\used_{\cal L})=\varcount(\cal F)$, and if $\cal L=\cal L^k_{\cal M,\rnd}$ then $\sum_{x} h^k_{\cal M,\rnd}(x)=\len(\used_{\cal L})$.
conclusions: if $\cal L=\cal L^k_{\cal M,\rnd}$: $\sum_{x\in V(G)} h^k_{\cal M,\rnd}(x)=\len(\used_{\cal L})$

nodes.name: Counting $\De$-labelled trees
nodes.statement: (a) $P_i\le (\me\De)^i$ where $P_i$ counts iso-classes of $\De$-labelled trees on $i$ vertices. (b) $R_{k,i}\le (i+1)^{k-1}(\me\De)^i$ counts $k$-tuples of trees with total size $i$.

nodes.name: Counting landscapes with fixed forest
nodes.statement: For finite $G$ and a $G$-forest $\cal F$ of finite height, the number of $\cal M$-landscapes $(\cal F,\prev)$ is at most $\be^{|V(\cal F)|}\cdot b^{\varcount(\cal F)-|V(G)|}$, where $\be=\max_x |\mathbf R^c(x)|/b^{|\Var(x)|}$.
conclusions: $\#\{\prev:(\cal F,\prev)$ is an $\cal M$-landscape$\}\le \be^{|V(\cal F)|}\cdot b^{\varcount(\cal F)-|V(G)|}$

nodes.name: Restriction preserves used bits at interior
nodes.statement: If $U\subset V(G)$ is $\pi$-unique and $x\in U$ with $\Var_G(\Cl_G(x))\cup \Cl_G(x)\subset U$, then $\used_{\cal L}(x)=\used_{\Res_U(\cal L)}(S_\pi(x))$.
assumptions: $\cal M=(G,\mathbf R,\pi)$, $\cal L$ a finalised $\cal M$-landscape

nodes.name: Reducing airborne trees
nodes.statement: For finite $G$, if $\cal L$ is a finalised $\cal M$-landscape with $|\Trees^\vee(\cal L)|>0$ then there exists an equivalent landscape $\cal L'$ with $|\Trees^\vee(\cal L')|<|\Trees^\vee(\cal L)|$.
assumptions: $\cal L$ a finalised $\cal M$-landscape with $|\Trees^\vee(\cal L)|>0$
conclusions: $\exists$ equivalent finalised $\cal M$-landscape $\cal L'$ with $|\Trees^\vee(\cal L')|<|\Trees^\vee(\cal L)|$

nodes.name: Subexponential growth lemma
nodes.statement:
If $|N(x,3
n)|\le (1+\eps)^{
n}$ for all $x$, $h:V(G)	o \NN$ bounded, and $h(y)$ is maximum, then there is $r\in\{3,\ldots,3
n\}$ with $\sum_{x\in N(y,r)} h(x)\le (1+\eps)\sum_{x\in N(y,r-3)} h(x)$.

nodes.name: Borel finite sparse partition exists
nodes.statement: For any Borel digraph $G=(V,\mathcal B,E)$ with bounded degrees and any $r\in \NN$, there is a Borel finite $r$-sparse partition of $V$.
assumptions: $G=(V,\mathcal B,E)$ Borel digraph with all degrees bounded

nodes.name: $r$-local Borel labellings stay Borel
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a Borel digraph with bounded degrees, $\ell$ a Borel countable-valued labelling, and $\ell'$ an $r$-local function of $(G,\ell)$. Then $\ell'$ is Borel.
assumptions: $\ell$ Borel labelling assuming countably many values

nodes.name: Borel maximal independent sets and Borel bad sets
nodes.statement: (a) Every Borel $A\subset V$ admits a Borel maximal independent subset $B\subset A$. (b) For Borel local rule $\mathbf R$ and Borel $f:V\to b$, the failed-clause set $B_{\mathbf R}(f)$ is Borel.
conclusions: (a) for every Borel $A\subset V$ there is Borel maximal independent $B\subset A$
(b) if $\mathbf R$ Borel and $f:V\to b$ Borel, then $B_{\mathbf R}(f)\subset V$ is Borel

nodes.name: Existence of equivalent grounded landscape
nodes.statement: For finite $G$ and any finalised $\cal M$-landscape $\cal L$, there exists a grounded finalised landscape $\cal K$ equivalent to $\cal L$.
conclusions: $\exists$ grounded finalised landscape $\cal K$ equivalent to $\cal L$

nodes.name: Counting grounded forests and finalised landscapes
nodes.statement: For finite $G$ and $\De=\maxdeg(\Rel(G))$: (a) the number of grounded $G$-forests with $|V(\cal F)|=m$ is at most $(m+1)^{|V(G)|-1}(\me\De)^m$; (b) for fixed $\cal F$ with $m,v$ as above, $\#(\prev,\final)\le \be^m b^v$.
conclusions: (a) $\#$ grounded $G$-forests with $|V(\cal F)|=m$ is at most $(m+1)^{|V(G)|-1}(\me\De)^m$
(b) given grounded $\cal F$ with $m=|V(\cal F)|$, $v=\varcount(\cal F)$, $\be=\max_x|\mathbf R^c(x)|/b^{|\Var(x)|}$: $\#\{(\prev,\final)\}\le \be^m b^v$

nodes.name: Parallel Moser-Tardos Algorithm (with shared randomness over $\pi$)
nodes.statement: Iterative parallel resampler that, given $(\cal M,\rnd)$ with $\cal M=(G,\mathbf R,\pi)$ and $\rnd\in b^{\pi\times \NN}$, produces colourings $\MT^0,\MT^1,\ldots$ by resampling variables of a maximal independent set of violated clauses each step using shared randomness across each part of $\pi$.

nodes.name: Sequential deterministic MTA via external/internal loops
nodes.statement: Linear-time deterministic algorithm: enumerate all candidate $\rnd_m\in b^{\pi\times m}$ in an external loop, simulate the parallel MTA in an internal loop using lists Currently-Violated and Potentially-Violated, abort branches that exhaust $\rnd_m$.

nodes.name: Original Moser-Tardos algorithm
nodes.statement: Randomised resampling algorithm of Moser-Tardos that, under the LLL gap condition, finds a satisfying assignment using $O(|V(G)|)$ random bits in expectation.
input: Colouring problem $(G,\mathbf R)$ satisfying LLL with constant slack

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2.c (linear-time deterministic)
nodes.statement: Build $3\nn$-sparse partition $\pi$ of size $\le d^{6\nn}$ via greedy power-graph colouring, choose $m$ from inequality (2.6), iterate over $\rnd_m\in b^{\pi\times m}$ running internal-loop simulation of parallel MTA; each pass uses lists Currently-Violated/Potentially-Violated.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1.1 (predecessor lemma)
nodes.statement: If no $(y,i)\in V(\cal F)$ shares a variable with $x$, then no variable of $x$ was resampled and $x\in \B(\MT^i)$; maximality of $\IB(\MT^i)$ then forces a neighbour, contradiction.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1.2 (length identities)
nodes.statement: Double counting on $V(\cal F)$ pairs $(x,(y,i))$ with $x\in \Var(y)$ gives $\len(\used_{\cal L})=\varcount(\cal F)$; combined with $h^k_{\cal M,\rnd}(x)=\len(\used^k_{\cal M,\rnd}(x))$ and Lemma 3.1.2 (used-equality) gives the second identity.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2 (counting $\De$-labelled trees)
nodes.statement: Use generating function $P(X)=\sum P_i X^i$, bound polynomial $Q_i(\rho)\le \De/(\De-1)$ inductively from $Q_{i+1}(X)=1+XQ_i(X)^\De$, deduce $P_i\le (\De^\De/(\De-1)^{\De-1})^i$ then convert via $(\De/(\De-1))^{\De-1}\le \me$. For (b), bound coefficients of $P(X)^k$ by induction.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2 (counting landscapes per forest)
nodes.statement: Multiply $|\mathbf R^c(x)|=(|\mathbf R^c(x)|/b^{|\Var(x)|})\cdot b^{|\Var(x)|}$ over $(x,i)\in V(\cal F)$ and apply $\sum_{(x,i)} |\Var(x)|=\varcount(\cal F)-|V(G)|$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3.2 (counting forests/landscapes)
nodes.statement: (a) Specifying a grounded forest of size $m$ amounts to picking, for each $x\in V(G)$, an iso-class of $\De$-labelled tree summing to $m$ vertices; bound by Lemma 3.2(b). (b) Combine Lemma 3.5 and $\final\in b^{V(G)}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3 (classical MTA)
nodes.statement: Recover $\rnd_k$ from $(\cal L^k_{\cal M,\rnd},\unused^k)$; bound $P_{m,v}$ by counting grounded landscapes (Corollary 3.2) and complementary $\unused$ functions (Remark 3.0); $P_m$ follows by summing $v\le dm+|V(G)|$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.4 (restriction preserves $\used$)
nodes.statement: When $\Var(\Cl(x))\cup \Cl(x)\subset U$, every $y$ with $x\in \Var(y)$ satisfies $\Var(y)\subset U$, so $\mathbf R'(S_\pi(y))$ and $\prev'(S_\pi(y),i)$ are obtained by composition with $T_U$; equality of $\used$ follows.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.5 (airborne reduction)
nodes.statement: Argue by contradiction with minimal counterexample $\cal L$ and minimal-size airborne tree $\tau$. Three cases: push $\tau$ down one level (Step 1); reroute non-root vertex $x$ (Step 2); reroute root $x$ (Step 3). Each yields equivalent landscape contradicting minimality.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.6 (subexponential growth)
Proof of Theorem 3.7 (main analysis)
nodes.statement: For each $\rnd$ pick max-resample vertex $y$ and radius $r$ via Lemma 3.6; restrict landscape to $N(y,r)$ and replace by grounded equivalent $\cal K_{\rnd}$; bound $P_{m,v}$ by enumerating $(\cal N,\cal K,\C)$ with constraint $\len_Y(\used_{\cal K})>(1-\eps)\len(\used_{\cal K})$; sum tail series.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4 (Borel LLL)
nodes.statement: Choose $\de>0$ realising the strict inequality, build a Borel $3\nn$-sparse partition $\pi$, apply Theorem 2.c almost surely $h^\infty<\infty$, fix such $\rnd$, show $\MT^k$ stabilises and $\MT^\infty$ is a Borel satisfying colouring.

nodes.name: Bounded $|\pi|$ via greedy colouring of $G^{6\nn}$
nodes.statement:
There is a $3
n$-sparse partition $\pi$ of $V(G)$ with $|\pi|\le d^{6
n}$, obtained by greedy proper colouring of the graph $H$ where vertices are joined iff at distance $\le 6
n$ in $G$.

nodes.name: Borel LLL fails on exponential-growth graphs
nodes.statement: Marks's Borel chromatic-number construction yields a $d$-regular acyclic Borel graph whose LLL instance has $p<1/(\me\De)$ but admits no Borel satisfying colouring; Conley et al strengthened this to hyperfinite graphs.

nodes.name: Push tree down one level (Step 1)
nodes.statement: If for all $(x,i)\in V(\tau)$ and $(y,i-1)\in V(\cal F)\setminus V(\tau)$ we have $\Var_G(x)\cap \Var_G(y)=\emptyset$, then push $\tau$ down one level; the resulting forest stays independent and $\used$ is preserved.

nodes.name: Reroute non-root vertex (Step 2)
nodes.statement: If $x$ is not the root of $\tau$ and there exist $(y,i-1)\in V(\cal F)\setminus V(\tau)$ with $\Var(x)\cap \Var(y)\neq \emptyset$: remove $x$'s incoming edge in $\tau$, add edge $((y,i-1),(x,i))$. This produces an equivalent landscape with a smaller airborne tree, contradicting minimality of $m_2$.

nodes.name: Reroute root vertex (Step 3)
nodes.statement: If $x$ is the root of $\tau$: add edge $((y,i-1),(x,i))$ to the forest. The resulting equivalent landscape has one less airborne tree than $\cal L$, contradicting minimality of $m_1$.

nodes.name: Choose maximally-resampled vertex and radius
nodes.statement: Fix $\rnd\in b^{\pi\times k}$, set $h:=h^k_{\cal M,\rnd}$, pick $y$ maximising $h$, apply Lemma 3.6 to obtain $r\in\{3,\ldots,3\nn\}$ with the boundary growth bound.

nodes.name: Restrict landscape to ball $N(y,r)$ and ground it
nodes.statement: Set $\cal N_{\rnd}:=\Res_{N(y,r)}(\cal M)$ and pick a grounded finalised $\cal N_{\rnd}$-landscape $\cal K_{\rnd}$ equivalent to $\Res_{N(y,r)}(\cal L^k_{\cal M,\rnd})$, using Proposition 3.5.

nodes.name: Recover $\rnd$ from $(\cal N_{\rnd},\cal K_{\rnd},\C_{\rnd})$
nodes.statement: Define $\C_{\rnd}:\pi\to b^{\oplus \NN}$ via $\unused$ on the interior and full $\rnd$ outside; using Lemma 3.4 and Lemma 3.1.2, $\rnd$ is recoverable from the triple, giving the union-bound inequality on $P_{m,v}$.

nodes.name: Bound $\#\cal N$, $\#(\cal K,\C)$ and combine
nodes.statement: Bound $\#\cal N\le (|\pi|^d 2^{b^d})^{|\pi|}$, $\#\cal K\le (m+1)^{|\pi|-1}/(\me\De)^{\delta m}\cdot b^{(1-\eps)v+\eps|\pi|}$ via Corollary 3.2 and the gap (3.5), and $\#\C\le 2^{|\pi|} b^{k|\pi|-(1-\eps)v}$ via the boundary inequality (3.10).

nodes.name: Sum tail series to conclude (3.11)
nodes.statement: Summing $\sum_{i\ge m} (i+1)^{|\pi|}/(\me\De)^{\de i}\le (m+1)^{|\pi|}/(\me\De)^{\de m}\cdot |\pi|!/(1-(\me\De)^{-\de})^{|\pi|}$ gives $\Pr_{\rnd}(|V(\cal K_{\rnd})|\ge m)\le K(m+1)^{|\pi|}/(\me\De)^{\de m}$.

nodes.name: Generating-function setup
nodes.statement: Define $P(X):=\sum_i P_i X^i$ and $\rho:=(\De-1)^{\De-1}/\De^\De$; reduce the bound to showing $P(\rho)\le \De/(\De-1)$.

nodes.name: Inductive bound $Q_i(\rho)\le \De/(\De-1)$
nodes.statement: Using $Q_{i+1}(X)=1+XQ_i(X)^\De$ and the inductive assumption, $Q_{i+1}(\rho)\le 1+\rho(\De/(\De-1))^\De=\De/(\De-1)$. Combined with $(\De/(\De-1))^{\De-1}\le \me$, conclude (a).

nodes.name: Bound $S_{k,i}$ inductively for part (b)
nodes.statement: Set $R_k(X)=P(X)^k$ bounded by $S_k(X)=(\sum_i (\me\De X)^i)^k$. Inductively show $S_{k,i}\le (i+1)^{k-1}(\me\De)^i$ via $S_{k+1,i}=\sum_j S_{k,j}(\me\De)^{i-j}$.

nodes.name: Initialise $\MT^0$
nodes.statement: $\MT^0(x):=\rnd(S_\pi(x),0)$ for all $x\in V(G)$; set $h^0\equiv 0$, $h^1\equiv 1$.

nodes.name: Iterative resampling loop
nodes.statement: For each $j\in \NN$: compute $\IB(\MT^j)$ (maximal independent subset of bad clauses in $\Rel(G)$); set $\MT^{j+1}(x):=\rnd(S_\pi(x),h^{j+1}(x))$ if $x\in \Var(\IB(\MT^j))$, else $\MT^j(x)$; increment $h^{j+2}$ accordingly.

nodes.name: Termination criterion
nodes.statement: The algorithm succeeds after $i$ steps if $\B(\MT^{i-1})=\emptyset$; output $\MT^{i-1}$, which then satisfies $\mathbf R$.

nodes.name: Build $3\nn$-sparse partition
nodes.statement:
Compute graph power $G^{6
n}$ and apply greedy vertex colouring to obtain a $3
n$-sparse partition $\pi$ of $V(G)$ with $|\pi|\le d^{6
n}$ in linear time.

nodes.name: External loop over $\rnd_m\in b^{\pi\times m}$
nodes.statement: For each candidate $\rnd_m$ in the constantly-many possibilities, run the internal loop; abort and move to the next $\rnd_m$ as soon as $\rnd(\ast,m)$ would be accessed.

nodes.name: Internal loop with Currently/Potentially-Violated lists
nodes.statement: Each pass: for $C\in$ Currently-Violated, resample $\Var(C)$ via $\rnd$ unless an already-resampled $\Rel(G)$-neighbour exists in this pass; then refresh Currently-Violated as the entries of old Potentially-Violated still violated, and Potentially-Violated as Currently-Violated together with their $\Rel(G)$-neighbours.

nodes.name: Output upon empty Currently-Violated
nodes.statement: Halt and output $\MT^i$ as the satisfying assignment when Currently-Violated becomes empty after some pass.
